column1: # THE RESULT, which reconciles all four prior attributions instead of adding a fifth.
# Cell 2 and cell 3 point OPPOSITE WAYS, and both are clean:
#   - Germany: English + organ = NIL.  German is NECESSARY.
#   - Brazil:  English + organ = PRODUCTIVE.  Portuguese is REDUNDANT.
# So the necessity of an in-language leg is NOT a property of the query, and NOT a property of
# the region.  It is a property of THE JURISDICTION'S OWN PUBLICATION CORPUS: Brazilian
# education policy is carried by English-language legal and business press (Mattos Filho
# publishes in English; an instrument NUMBER is a language-independent token), German school
# policy is not carried in English at all.
# This is why four passes found four different axes: each sampled different jurisdictions.
#   PJ  sampled Brazil, Mexico, Quebec -- all with English-language legal press -> "language did nothing"
#   372 sampled Germany                -- no English corpus                     -> "language is the axis"
# BOTH ARE LOCALLY CORRECT AND NEITHER GENERALISES.  A single global rule will be wrong in one
# direction or the other for some jurisdiction, in BOTH directions, which is what has happened.
